events.title: Death of Captain James Cook
events.description: British explorer Captain James Cook was killed during a confrontation with native Hawaiians at Kealakekua Bay on the island of Hawaii, during his third voyage to the Pacific.
events.significance: Cook's voyages charted much of the Pacific, including Australia's east coast, New Zealand, and Hawaii, greatly expanding European geographic knowledge and shaping later colonial expansion.

events.title: Bell and Gray File Telephone Patent Applications
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell filed a patent application for the telephone at the U.S. Patent Office in Washington, D.C., on the same day that Elisha Gray filed a caveat for a similar device.
events.significance: Bell's patent, granted on March 7, 1876, became one of the most valuable in history, launching modern telecommunications and sparking long-running legal disputes over invention priority.

events.title: Birth of Frederick Douglass (traditionally observed)
events.description: Frederick Douglass, born into slavery in Maryland, chose February 14 as his birthday since he did not know his exact birth date. He escaped slavery in 1838 and became a leading abolitionist, orator, writer, and statesman.
events.significance: Douglass became one of the most influential African American leaders of the 19th century, advocating for abolition, women's suffrage, and equal rights, and advising President Abraham Lincoln.

events.title: Arizona Admitted as the 48th U.S. State
events.description: Arizona was admitted to the Union as the 48th state, becoming the last of the contiguous United States to achieve statehood.
events.significance: Arizona's admission completed the continental expansion of the United States, ending a long process of territorial organization in the American Southwest.

events.title: St. Valentine's Day Massacre
events.description: Seven members and associates of Chicago's North Side Gang were gunned down in a garage by assailants, some disguised as police officers, in an attack widely attributed to Al Capone's organization.
events.significance: The massacre shocked the nation, intensified public and federal pressure against organized crime during Prohibition, and contributed to Capone's eventual downfall.
